question: Should FixedToolbar measure itself and mutate an editor scroll container, or should copied editor layout eliminate the overlap?
trigger: User asks whether the FixedToolbar working-tree diff is dirty and requests the cleanest architecture through Best API Review.
requirements: Keep a fixed toolbar visible without obscuring the editor's caret or generated content.
Preserve a shared toolbar with no selected editor and manual toolbars outside EditorContainer.
Keep copied layout policy out of Plite and preserve the existing neutral CSS scroll-padding behavior.
Review only; do not implement the downstream layout migration.
evidenceReuse: Rechecked the current diff, actual internal/external/shared consumers, the padding test, container registration, throwing editor lookup and Plite's CSS-padding reader. Prior AI preview ownership and completed docs-embed behavior receipts are context, not proof of toolbar ownership. First focused review; broader UI remains unassessed.
summary: Pursue deleting the FixedToolbar editor subscription, ResizeObserver and inline-padding save/restore protocol by making the copied panel allocate a toolbar row outside the actual content scrollport.
alternatives: Keep/configure: the current effect assumes every toolbar obstructs the selected editor scrollport, contradicted by external and shared consumers.
Change API: optional editor lookup or a reusable measuring hook can avoid one failure but preserves incorrect placement and style ownership.
Add primitive: a toolbar obstruction registry or new Plite scrolling API is unnecessary; the substrate already honors CSS scroll padding.
Delete/merge: remove the overlap and all height synchronization from the default composition; retain presentational FixedToolbar and its kit plugin for their current independent jobs.
Move ownership: copied editor layout owns height and scroll placement; beforeContainer is an existing slot for toolbar placement when used inside the appropriate outer frame.

Replace architecture: a flex/grid panel with a non-scrolling toolbar row and a shrinking content scroll area removes the protocol entirely. CSS scroll padding remains an escape for deliberately overlapping custom UI.
proofLimits: Source review only; no browser or performance run for a replacement. The mocked toolbar test asserts the chosen implementation protocol, not containment or selected-editor availability. Proposed layout still needs bounded/page scrolling, shared-toolbar startup, zoom/custom heights, selection and exact AI menu replay. No new JavaScript runtime machinery or speed claim is accepted. Broad UI and AI scope proof statuses are unchanged.
